issues.legal_issue: A statutory development authority cannot be compelled to reconvey acquired land when the governing statute and rules do not authorize reconveyance.
material_facts: The land was acquired for a development scheme, possession was taken, and compensation was paid or deposited.
The predecessor authority resolved to reconvey part of the land, but the resolution was not implemented.
The authority later formed and allotted sites on the land in accordance with the development scheme.
The landowner sought a writ directing reconveyance based on the resolution.
issues.conclusion: The authority had no power under the governing legislation to reconvey the acquired land, and no direction to reconvey it could be issued.
issues.legal_principle: The City of Bangalore Improvement Act, 1945, Section 29(2), required acquired land to be applied for the improvement scheme and made the power to transfer sites subject to prescribed rules; the applicable rules did not authorize reconveyance. The Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, likewise did not confer a general power to reconvey acquired land. The Court relied on B.N. Sathyanarayana Rao v. State of Karnataka, A.V. Lakshman v. B.D.A., and Rachappa v. State. It explained that Muniyappa v. Bangalore Development Authority concerned an allotment under Rule 5, not reconveyance, and affirmed that the authority lacked power to reconvey land acquired for a scheme.

rule.if: writ_claim_for_reconveyance and land_acquired_for_public_development and possession_taken and not statutory_power_to_reconvey

predicates.writ_claim_for_reconveyance: A person sought a writ requiring a public development authority to return land acquired for a development scheme.
predicates.land_acquired_for_public_development: The land was acquired to carry out a public development scheme.
predicates.possession_taken: The acquiring authority took possession of the land.
predicates.statutory_power_to_reconvey: The governing law authorized the authority to reconvey the acquired land.

issues.definition: When a writ claim seeks return of land acquired for public development, possession has been taken, and the law grants no reconveyance power, the authority cannot be compelled to return the land.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel cannot require a public authority to carry out a promise that it lacks legal power to perform.
material_facts: The predecessor authority adopted a resolution promising to reconvey part of the acquired land subject to conditions.
In reliance on the proposed arrangement, the landowner withdrew compensation-reference proceedings and did not pursue compensation in the ordinary course.
The governing legislation did not authorize the authority to reconvey the acquired land.
The landowner relied on the promise to argue that the authority was barred from resiling from it.
issues.conclusion: Promissory estoppel could not be used to compel the authority to reconvey land contrary to the governing law.
issues.legal_principle: Promissory estoppel may bind a public authority where a clear promise is intended to be acted on and the promisee changes position, but it cannot compel an act prohibited by law or beyond the authority's power. The Court relied on Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh, A.P. Pollution Control Board II v. Prof. M.V. Nayudu, Sharma Transport v. Government of A.P., and Pune Municipal Corporation v. Promoters and Builders Association. It distinguished State of Punjab v. Nestle India Ltd., where the authority had statutory power to grant the promised exemption.

rule.if: public_authority_promise_dispute and clear_promise_made and promisee_changed_position and promised_act_not_authorized_by_law

predicates.public_authority_promise_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a public authority must honor a promise it made.
predicates.clear_promise_made: The authority made a clear promise intended to be acted on by the recipient.
predicates.promisee_changed_position: The recipient acted on the promise and changed position to their detriment.
predicates.promised_act_not_authorized_by_law: The authority lacked legal power to perform the promised act.

issues.definition: If a public authority makes a clear promise that is acted on to the recipient's detriment, but the authority lacks power to perform it, the promise cannot be enforced through promissory estoppel.

issues.legal_issue: Acquired land cannot be released from acquisition after possession has been taken and the land has vested in the State.
material_facts: An award was made and possession of the land was taken after the award.
The land consequently vested in the State and was transferred to the development authority.
The proposed release or reconveyance was sought after possession and vesting had occurred.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition could not be withdrawn or cancelled after possession had been taken and the land had vested in the State.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 16, 48, and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, taking possession after the award vests the land absolutely in the State, and the acquisition process is complete once compensation is tendered and possession is taken. Section 48 does not permit withdrawal after vesting, and Section 21 of the General Clauses Act cannot be used to undo that statutory vesting. The Court relied on Lt. Governor of Himachal Pradesh v. Sri Avinash Sharma, Pratap v. State of Rajasthan, Mohan Singh v. International Airport Authority of India, and Printers (Mysore) Ltd. v. M.A. Rasheed.

rule.if: acquisition_withdrawal_dispute and award_made and possession_taken and land_vested_in_state

predicates.acquisition_withdrawal_dispute: The proceeding seeks to release or withdraw land from a completed acquisition.
predicates.award_made: The acquiring authority made an award for the land.
predicates.possession_taken: The acquiring authority took possession of the land.
predicates.land_vested_in_state: The land vested in the State following the taking of possession.

issues.definition: In a dispute seeking withdrawal from an acquisition, an award, possession, and vesting in the State mean the acquisition cannot be withdrawn.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to allot a site to a former landowner does not authorize withdrawal of the acquisition or reconveyance of the acquired land.
material_facts: The authority's resolution to reconvey the land was made before the statutory amendment that created a limited power to allot sites to former owners.
No allotment to the landowner had been made within the period covered by the amendment's validation provision.
The landowner sought return of the acquired land itself, rather than allotment of a site formed under the scheme.
The High Court treated the statutory amendment and an earlier decision concerning allotment as supporting reconveyance.
issues.conclusion: The statutory provision authorized qualifying site allotments, not release or reconveyance of acquired land; its validation provision did not cover the earlier resolution.
issues.legal_principle: Section 38-C of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, authorized allotment by sale or lease of a site formed in scheme land in specified circumstances and subject to conditions; it did not authorize withdrawal of acquisition or reconveyance of the land itself. Section 9 of the Amendment Act validated qualifying allotments made during its specified period, but did not validate the earlier resolution at issue. The Court distinguished H.C. Venkataswamy v. Bangalore Development Authority, which concerned allotment of sites, and clarified that Muniyappa concerned a Rule 5 allotment rather than reconveyance.

predicates.claim_based_on_site_allotment_provision: A claimant relies on a statutory provision allowing a former landowner to receive a site formed in scheme land.
predicates.requested_relief_is_return_of_acquired_l: The claimant seeks return of the acquired land itself rather than allotment of a site formed under the scheme.
predicates.resolution_outside_validation_period: The resolution relied on was made outside the period covered by the statutory validation of earlier allotments.

issues.definition: Where a claim relies on a provision for site allotment but seeks return of the acquired land, and the relied-on resolution falls outside the validation period, the allotment power does not authorize release of the land.

issues.legal_issue: A government direction to a statutory development authority is binding only when it is authorized and directed toward carrying out the authority's statutory purposes.
material_facts: A communication issued on behalf of the government, based on a note from the Chief Minister, directed the authority to reconvey the land.
The direction relied on a High Court judgment that was set aside in this appeal.
The authority disputed the direction because reconveyance was contrary to the governing legislation and the purposes of the development scheme.
The Court found no showing that the Chief Minister was authorized to issue the direction and stated that a government order must conform to Article 166 of the Constitution.
issues.conclusion: The direction to reconvey the land was not binding because it was unauthorized and contrary to the statutory purposes of the authority.
issues.legal_principle: Section 65 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, permits government directions only when they are necessary or expedient for carrying out the Act's purposes; the authority is not bound by directions contrary to the Act. A government order must also conform to Article 166 of the Constitution. The Court additionally relied on the principle in Commissioner of Police, Bombay v. Gordhandas Bhanji and Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner that the validity of a public order is assessed objectively by the order and its stated grounds.

rule.if: statutory_authority_direction_dispute and direction_orders_return_of_acquired_land and direction_not_authorized and direction_conflicts_with_statutory_purpose

predicates.statutory_authority_direction_dispute: The dispute concerns a government direction to a statutory authority.
predicates.direction_orders_return_of_acquired_land: The direction tells the authority to return land acquired for its statutory development work.
predicates.direction_not_authorized: The person or body issuing the direction lacked authority to issue it in the required manner.
predicates.direction_conflicts_with_statutory_purpo: The direction would obstruct rather than carry out the purposes for which the authority was established.

issues.definition: A direction to a statutory authority to return acquired land is not binding when it was not properly authorized and conflicts with the authority's statutory purpose.

issues.legal_issue: Equitable compensation may be awarded when a landowner gave up compensation claims in reliance on an unenforceable reconveyance promise.
material_facts: The landowner withdrew proceedings seeking enhanced compensation after the authority proposed reconveyance.
The landowner did not pursue compensation that would otherwise have been available for the land.
Reconveyance could not lawfully be ordered because the acquisition was complete and the authority lacked power to return the land.
The Court balanced the equities by directing payment of the compensation due, including applicable enhancement, statutory benefits, and interest.
issues.conclusion: The landowner was entitled to reclaim compensation with applicable enhancement, statutory benefits, and interest, even though reconveyance was refused.
issues.legal_principle: The Court balanced the equities where the landowner had foregone compensation proceedings in reliance on the proposed reconveyance but the land could not lawfully be returned. It directed payment of the compensation determined by the acquiring authority together with any applicable enhancement and statutory benefits, and interest. The remedy was equitable relief in the circumstances of the case, not enforcement of the unlawful promise.

predicates.appeal_from_reconveyance_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an order directing reconveyance of acquired land.
predicates.reconveyance_unavailable_by_law: The acquired land cannot lawfully be reconveyed in the circumstances.
predicates.landowner_abandoned_compensation_claims_: The landowner gave up or failed to pursue compensation claims because of reliance on a proposed reconveyance.

issues.definition: If reconveyance is legally unavailable and a landowner abandoned compensation claims in reliance on its promise, the landowner may receive the compensation and applicable interest.
